articles.titleZh: 十二枚磁片和一封邮件
articles.summaryZh: 唐悠想省下半天课程准备时间，凭堆肥报告取消一次核查。写讲义时，一个问题让她停在了发送键前。
storyParagraphsZh: 屋顶农园准备换上春季课程用的一批展示盆，唐悠负责把课程材料和日程一起定下来。堆肥供应资料上列着总氮信息，她原本想据此取消已经排好的养分状态核查，把那半天留给别的课程准备。可她在写讲义时卡住了：报告告诉她“总共有多少”，却没有直接告诉她这些氮此刻有多少处在植物能够利用的形态。
她把取消核查的邮件留在草稿箱里，转去整理周末的课堂示意。桌上的堆肥样品和供应资料被放到一边。唐悠另外拿出十二枚磁片，在白板上画了三个框，写下“课堂模型”，再把磁片摆进去。
模型开始时，十二个氮单位被分成三处：土壤有机氮8单位、土壤中当期可利用的无机氮3单位、植株氮1单位。唐悠把其中2个单位从有机氮移到可利用氮，三个框变成6、5、1；接着又把1个单位从可利用氮移进植株，变成6、4、2。她每移动一次都重新数一遍，十二枚磁片一枚也没有增加。
她看着那十二枚磁片，又回到电脑前，把取消核查的邮件删掉了。她在日程上保留了那半天，把堆肥资料夹在核查安排后面。原本想提前完成的课程材料，只好留到下午继续做。
周末上课时，他们重新按8、3、1摆好磁片，先从土壤有机氮移2枚到可利用框，再由一个学生把1枚从“可利用”框移进“植株”框。此时“植株”里有2枚，另外两个框合起来还有10枚；他从头数到尾，抬头说：“还是十二个。”唐悠点点头，把真实展示盆推到白板旁边，却没有给它贴上那组数字：“这十二个是我们用来想清楚过程的，不是这盆土的化验单。”
articles.overallZh: 本篇用一次课程准备说明养分循环的一个小入口：元素可以在土壤有机物、植物可利用形态和生物体之间移动、转化和储存，因此土壤或堆肥中的总氮并不等于某一时刻植物可利用的氮。转化和吸收改变的是氮所在的形态和库，不会凭空创造新的氮。
explanationParagraphsZh: 12单位算例是一个与真实盆土分开的封闭教学时段模型，明确假设这一时段没有外部氮输入、输出或损失。三个账户互不重叠：土壤有机氮不计植株氮，土壤可利用库只计这里假设可被植物利用的无机氮，植株氮另计。开始分别为8、3、1，总量12；其中2单位由有机氮转到可利用氮后变为6、5、1，总量仍12；随后植物吸收1单位，可利用氮减少1、植株增加1，变成6、4、2，总量仍为12。这里的单位、转化量和顺序只是教学记账，不是实测值或真实矿化速率。
现实土壤中，有机氮能否以及多快转化为植物可利用形态，会受到材料性质、微生物活动和环境条件影响。开放农田还会有外部投入、收获带走、淋失和气态损失等路径。叶黄也可能与水分、温度、病害等因素有关，因此不能仅凭叶色或堆肥存在就判断植物当期缺氮或可利用氮充足；氮的这些过程也不能直接当作磷或所有元素完全相同的循环方式。

moduleZh.intro: 先把“总共有多少氮”与“氮此时在哪个库、植物现在能利用多少”分开，再追踪一次转化和一次吸收。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么12单位氮移动了两次，总量仍然是12
diagramSteps: 建立一个无外部输入、输出或损失的封闭教学时段，总氮设为12单位
把12单位分进互不重叠的三库：土壤有机氮8、土壤可利用无机氮3、植株氮1
让2单位由有机氮转到可利用氮，得到6、5、1
再让植物从可利用氮库吸收1单位，得到6、4、2
重新相加得到6+4+2=12，并把这个模型与真实展示盆的未知状态分开
diagramStepNotes: 封闭条件只是为了追踪元素守恒的教学简化，现实农田通常存在输入、输出和损失。
总氮12不等于可利用氮12；开始时本模型中可利用库只有3单位。
2单位发生的是库和形态变化，不是新增2单位氮，也不代表现实固定矿化比例。
植物吸收后植株库从1增到2，可利用库从5减到4，因此植株外其余两个库合计为10。
真实盆土的总量、形态和转化速率需要实际信息，本模型不能替代实测或农事判断。
mapping: 土壤有机氮8→6 → 教学模型中一部分氮从有机库转出。
可利用氮3→5→4 → 先接受2单位转化，再被植物吸收1单位。
植株氮1→2 → 植物从可利用库获得1单位氮。
总量始终12 → 在封闭教学时段内，转化和吸收没有创造或消灭氮。
保留养分状态核查 → 不用总氮信息替代植物当期可利用状态的问题。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只用氮展示养分循环中的一个小机制。总氮不等于植物当期可利用氮，有机氮转化需要合适的材料、环境和微生物条件。12单位模型明确假设一个封闭时段内无外部输入、输出或损失，不能当成真实盆土、农田数据、矿化速率或施肥依据。现实系统还会有收获带走、淋失、气态损失等路径，氮与磷等元素的循环机制也不能简单视为完全相同。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果有人在这个模型中从外部加入2个氮单位，总量还应固定为12吗？你会怎样记录外部输入，并继续区分总量与当期可利用量？

referencesZh.citation: University of Minnesota Extension. (n.d.). Soil organic matter in cropping systems.
referencesZh.use: 支持有机物分解及微生物矿化、固定等过程会影响氮的形态与植物可利用性，并且转化速度受材料和环境条件影响；本篇只以氮为入口，不把虚构12单位模型或其中2单位转化当作来源数据或通用释放比例。

referencesZh.citation: Minnesota Department of Agriculture. (n.d.). Nitrogen Management.
referencesZh.use: 支持氮在有机形态、无机可利用形态和植物之间发生转化与吸收，同时现实农业系统还存在收获带走、淋失和气态损失等路径；本篇不据此提供施肥剂量、真实田间数值或产量保证。

articles.title: Twelve Tokens and an Email
articles.summary: Tang You hopes to save half a day of class preparation by using a compost report to cancel a check. While writing the handout, a question stops her before she sends the email.
storyParagraphs: The rooftop garden is preparing a new set of display pots for its spring classes, and Tang You is responsible for finalizing both the teaching materials and the schedule. The compost supplier's documentation includes total-nitrogen information, and she originally plans to use that to cancel an already scheduled nutrient-status check and free up half a day for other course preparation. But while writing the handout, she stops: the report tells her 'how much there is in total,' not directly how much of that nitrogen is currently in forms the plants can use.

She leaves the cancellation email in her drafts and turns to preparing the weekend classroom demonstration. She sets the compost sample and supplier documentation to one side. Then she takes out twelve magnetic tokens, draws three boxes on the whiteboard, writes “classroom model” above them, and puts the tokens in place.

At the start of the model, the twelve nitrogen units are divided among three places: 8 units in soil organic nitrogen, 3 in currently plant-available mineral nitrogen in the soil, and 1 in the plant. Tang You moves 2 units from organic nitrogen to the available-nitrogen box, giving 6, 5, 1. Then she moves 1 unit from available nitrogen into the plant, giving 6, 4, 2. Each time she moves the tokens, she counts again; not one of the twelve tokens has been added.

She looks at the twelve tokens, returns to her computer, and deletes the cancellation email. She keeps the half-day appointment in the schedule and files the compost documentation behind the check arrangements. The teaching materials she had hoped to finish early will have to wait until the afternoon.

During the weekend class, they reset the tokens to 8, 3, 1. First they move 2 from soil organic nitrogen into the available box, then a student moves 1 from 'available' into 'plant'. There are now 2 tokens in 'plant' and 10 in the other two boxes combined. He counts from the beginning and looks up: “Still twelve.” Tang You nods and wheels the real display pot beside the whiteboard without attaching those numbers to it. “These twelve help us think through the process. They are not a laboratory report for this pot.”
articles.overall: This article uses one course-preparation decision to introduce a small entry point into nutrient cycling: an element can move, transform, and be stored among soil organic matter, plant-available forms, and living organisms, so total nitrogen in soil or compost is not the same as the amount of nitrogen available to plants at a particular moment. Transformation and uptake change the form and pool in which nitrogen resides; they do not create new nitrogen from nothing.
explanationParagraphs: The 12-unit example is a closed teaching-period model kept separate from the real potting material. It explicitly assumes that during this period there are no external nitrogen inputs, outputs, or losses. The three accounts do not overlap: soil organic nitrogen excludes plant nitrogen, the soil available pool contains mineral nitrogen assumed available to the plant, and plant nitrogen is counted separately. They begin at 8, 3, and 1 units respectively, totaling 12. When 2 units move from organic nitrogen to available nitrogen, the state becomes 6, 5, 1 and still totals 12. The plant then takes up 1 unit, so available nitrogen decreases by 1 and plant nitrogen increases by 1, giving 6, 4, 2, again totaling 12. The units, conversion amount, and sequence are teaching bookkeeping, not measured values or a real mineralization rate.

In real soil, whether and how quickly organic nitrogen becomes plant-available depends on material properties, microbial activity, and environmental conditions. Open agricultural systems also include pathways such as external inputs, nitrogen removal through harvest, leaching, and gaseous losses. Yellow leaves may also result from water conditions, temperature, disease, or other factors, so leaf colour or the presence of compost alone cannot determine whether a plant is currently nitrogen-deficient or has sufficient available nitrogen. These nitrogen processes also should not be assumed to operate identically for phosphorus or every other element.

module.intro: First separate 'how much nitrogen exists in total' from 'which pool it is in now and how much plants can currently use,' then trace one conversion and one uptake step.
module.diagramTitle: Why Does the Total Stay at 12 Even After the 12 Nitrogen Units Move Twice?
diagramSteps: Set up a closed teaching period with no external inputs, outputs, or losses and define total nitrogen as 12 units
Divide 12 units among three non-overlapping pools: soil organic nitrogen 8, soil available mineral nitrogen 3, and plant nitrogen 1
Move 2 units from organic nitrogen to available nitrogen, producing 6, 5, 1
Then let the plant take up 1 unit from the available pool, producing 6, 4, 2
Add the pools again to obtain 6+4+2=12 and keep this model separate from the unknown state of the real display pot
diagramStepNotes: The closed condition is only a teaching simplification for tracking conservation of the element; real agricultural systems usually have inputs, outputs, and losses.
Total nitrogen of 12 does not mean 12 units are plant-available; at the beginning of this model, only 3 units are in the available pool.
The 2 units undergo a change of pool and form; they are not 2 newly created units of nitrogen and do not represent a universal real-world mineralization proportion.
After plant uptake, the plant pool rises from 1 to 2 while the available pool falls from 5 to 4, so the two pools outside the plant together contain 10.
The real pot's total amount, forms, and transformation rates require actual information; this model cannot substitute for measurement or agronomic judgment.
mapping: Soil organic nitrogen 8→6 → part of the nitrogen moves out of the organic pool in the teaching model.
Available nitrogen 3→5→4 → the pool first receives 2 units from conversion and then loses 1 unit to plant uptake.
Plant nitrogen 1→2 → the plant receives 1 unit from the available pool.
Total always 12 → within the closed teaching period, conversion and uptake neither create nor destroy nitrogen.
Keeping the nutrient-status check → not using total-nitrogen information as a substitute for the question of current plant availability.
module.boundary: This article uses nitrogen only to illustrate one small mechanism within nutrient cycling. Total nitrogen is not the same as nitrogen currently available to plants, and conversion of organic nitrogen requires suitable material, environmental, and microbial conditions. The 12-unit model explicitly assumes a closed period with no external inputs, outputs, or losses and cannot be treated as real potting-soil data, field data, a mineralization rate, or a fertilization basis. Real systems also include removal through harvest, leaching, gaseous losses, and other pathways, and the cycling mechanisms of nitrogen and phosphorus or other elements should not be treated as identical.
module.reflection: If someone adds 2 nitrogen units from outside this model, should the total still stay at 12? How would you record that input while continuing to distinguish total nitrogen from nitrogen currently available to plants?

references.citation: University of Minnesota Extension. (n.d.). Soil organic matter in cropping systems.
references.use: Supports that organic-matter decomposition and microbial processes such as mineralization and immobilization affect nitrogen forms and plant availability, and that transformation rates depend on material and environmental conditions. This article uses nitrogen only as an entry point and does not treat the fictional 12-unit model or the 2-unit conversion as source data or a universal release proportion.

references.citation: Minnesota Department of Agriculture. (n.d.). Nitrogen Management.
references.use: Supports nitrogen transformation and uptake among organic forms, inorganic plant-available forms, and plants, while real agricultural systems also include pathways such as harvest removal, leaching, and gaseous loss. This article does not use the source to provide fertilizer rates, real field values, or yield guarantees.

articles.summaryZh: 周末采摘前，何淼在入口旁发现新叶孔。整片处理的单子已经准备好了，她却还需要弄清这些痕迹意味着什么。
storyParagraphsZh: 社区菜园周六要开放采摘，何淼周四巡园时发现入口旁一排叶菜上多了几处新叶孔。她负责决定要不要启动已经准备好的虫害处理安排。距离开放只剩两天，如果损伤正在继续，她不能装作没看见；可要是一看到叶孔就把整片都纳入处理，周末的采摘区也得跟着改。
她沿着菜畦逐株看过去，在出现新鲜缺口的位置夹上小标记。越往里走，很多叶孔的边缘已经干了，像是早些时候留下的；两片叶背还有她认不准的小虫。何淼没有把那些虫直接当成答案，而是记下位置和外形，让负责植保判断的同事继续识别，同时把当天的新鲜损伤集中在哪一段记录下来。
第二天早晨，标记先给了她一半答案：新的啃食仍集中在入口附近那一小段，其他区域没有出现同样的增加。补充检查随后在同一小段确认了仍在活动、且取食痕迹与这些新伤相符的害物；前一天拍到的两只小虫则不是这次处理判断的依据。何淼原本准备填写的整片处理单因此作废，改成只核对这一小段是否达到既定计划中的行动条件。
这一小段最终达到干预条件，植保同事先比较适用控制办法的有效性，以及对人员、周围植物和环境的风险，再按原先专业计划确定局部方案。何淼让选定的防治只在相应位置执行，并安排之后复查新损伤是否继续。入口旁堆着的旧周转箱也被移回正常存放处，日常整理照常进行。周六开放时，这一小段继续封闭，不进入当天采摘路线；其他区域则按原活动安排管理。
周六早晨，志愿者把采摘指示牌一路摆到入口，在那一小段前停了下来。何淼把最后一块箭头牌往旁边挪，让路线绕过仍挂着复查标记的菜畦。旧叶孔还留在几片叶子上，她没有去数它们，只蹲下来翻开前一天标记的那几株，看有没有新的啃食。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：虫害管理不是见到损伤就整片行动，而是让识别、监测、预防、行动界线、针对性控制和复查连续影响下一步判断。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例先区分旧伤和正在增加的新伤，再把害物识别与损伤位置对应起来。前一天看到的身份不明昆虫没有被直接当作处理依据；只有在同一局部确认仍有与新损伤相符的活动害物，并且达到既定情境计划中的行动条件后，人物才进入针对性控制。
达到行动条件之后，仍要比较适用控制办法的有效性和对人员、其他生物及环境的风险；“只处理一小段”本身还不足以说明选对了办法。
综合虫害管理不是单纯少处理、不处理或等待害物自行消失。行动界线会随作物、害物、生育阶段、健康与管理情境而变化；预防性环境整理也不能被误写成已经证明某个具体虫源。控制后还需要复查效果和新损伤。本例不提供通用阈值、药品、剂量、食品安全结论或现实操作方案。

moduleZh.intro: 先弄清正在发生什么，再判断是否已经达到需要行动的程度；预防、控制与复查都由新的现场信息继续修正。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么发现叶孔后，何淼没有立刻处理整片菜畦
diagramSteps: 区分旧叶孔与新鲜损伤，并记录新损伤集中在哪些位置
继续识别现场昆虫，确认哪些观察与当前新损伤真正相关
同时整理容易造成管理混乱的环境条件，但不把整理本身当成虫源证明
将已确认的局部害物活动和损伤变化与既定行动条件比较；达到条件后，再比较适用办法的有效性与风险，确定针对性控制
控制后继续复查是否还有新的损伤，并据此决定下一步是否维持、调整或结束干预
diagramStepNotes: 一个叶孔不能说明整批植物正在遭遇同一种当前危害，旧伤与新伤需要分开。
看到昆虫不等于已经找到造成损伤的害物；识别必须与损伤类型、位置和持续活动相互对应。
预防和环境整理属于管理的一部分，但未经证据不能宣称某个箱子、角落或设施就是虫源。
行动界线依具体作物、害物、阶段和健康情境而定，本例没有提供可普遍照用的数字。
复查使管理形成循环；如果损伤继续、停止或出现新的信息，下一步行动都可能改变。
mapping: 干边旧叶孔 → 过去损伤，不自动代表当前问题仍在扩大。
入口附近持续出现的新啃食 → 需要继续调查和监测的当前变化。
确认与新伤相符的活动害物 → 把身份识别与当前损伤联系起来的关键信息。
局部达到既定行动条件 → 从观察进入针对性控制的决策点。
周六仍保留复查标记 → 控制之后继续检查效果，而不是把一次行动当作结束。
moduleZh.boundary: 综合虫害管理不是固定地少用药、从不用药或永远先等待。某些情境可能需要迅速行动，但是否行动以及采用什么控制方式，应依害物身份、作物和生育阶段、损伤发展、健康情境及既定专业计划判断。单个叶孔、身份未明昆虫或一次环境整理都不能替代这些信息。本故事不提供现实农药、剂量、安全间隔、采摘许可、食品安全认证或完整植保方案。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果下一次巡查发现同样数量的旧叶孔，但没有新的损伤，同时原先确认的害物活动也不再出现，你会期待管理者继续原来的控制，还是先改变下一步判断？为什么？

referencesZh.citation: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. (2026, July 22, updated). Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Principles.
referencesZh.use: 支持以行动界线、监测与识别、预防、多种控制方法和结果检查形成信息驱动的虫害管理循环，并支持在需要时合理采用控制措施；本篇只借用这一决策框架，不把任何虚构现场情节写成EPA案例，也不提供统一阈值、具体药品、剂量或全球通用操作规范。

articles.title: The Section They Walked Around
articles.summary: Before the weekend harvest event, He Miao finds fresh holes in leaves near the entrance. The form for treating the whole area is ready, but she still needs to find out what the damage means.
storyParagraphs: The community garden is due to open for harvesting on Saturday, and during her Thursday inspection He Miao notices several fresh holes on a row of leafy vegetables near the entrance. She is responsible for deciding whether to start the pest-control arrangement already prepared. Only two days remain before opening. If the damage is continuing, she cannot pretend not to see it; but if every visible hole causes the whole area to be included in treatment, the weekend harvesting area will have to change as well.

She works along the bed plant by plant, clipping small markers where she sees fresh missing edges. Farther along, many of the holes have already dried around the edges and look older; two leaves also carry small insects she cannot identify. He Miao does not treat those insects as the answer. She records their location and appearance, asks the colleague responsible for plant-protection assessment to continue the identification, and separately records the section in which that day's fresh damage is concentrated.

On Friday morning, the markers give her half the answer first: new feeding remains concentrated in that small section near the entrance, while the rest of the area shows no comparable increase. A follow-up inspection then confirms, in the same section, active pests whose feeding signs match the fresh damage; the two insects photographed the day before are not used as the basis for the treatment decision. The whole-area treatment form He Miao had been preparing is therefore discarded, and she instead checks only this small section against the action conditions in the pre-established plan.

That small section ultimately meets the intervention conditions, so the plant-protection colleague first compares suitable control methods for effectiveness and risks to people, nearby plants, and the environment, then selects a local approach under the existing professional plan. He Miao has the chosen control carried out only at the relevant locations, with a later check scheduled to see whether fresh damage continues. The old transport crates stacked near the entrance are returned to their usual storage place as routine housekeeping continues. When the garden opens on Saturday, this small section remains closed and is excluded from the day's harvesting route; the other areas continue under the original event arrangement.

On Saturday morning, volunteers place the harvesting signs along the entrance route and stop at the small closed section. He Miao shifts the last arrow sign to the side so the route goes around the bed that still carries the follow-up markers. Old holes remain on several leaves, but she does not count them. She crouches beside the plants marked the day before and checks whether there is any new feeding.
articles.overall: This article explains that pest management is not simply a matter of seeing damage and acting across the whole area. Identification, monitoring, prevention, action thresholds, targeted control, and follow-up inspection should continuously shape the next decision.
explanationParagraphs: This example first separates older damage from damage that is still increasing, then links pest identification to the location of the fresh damage. The unidentified insects seen on the first day are not used directly as a treatment basis. Targeted control begins only after the same local area is confirmed to contain active pests consistent with the new damage and the pre-established action conditions for that context are met.

Once action is warranted, suitable control methods still need to be compared for effectiveness and risks to people, other organisms, and the environment. Treating only a small area does not by itself establish that the method is appropriate.

Integrated pest management does not simply mean treating less, never treating, or waiting for pests to disappear on their own. Action thresholds vary with the crop, pest, growth stage, health context, and management situation. Preventive environmental housekeeping also cannot be rewritten as proof that a particular source of pests has been found. Control should be followed by checks on effectiveness and fresh damage. This example provides no universal threshold, pesticide, dose, food-safety conclusion, or real-world operating procedure.

module.intro: First determine what is actually happening, then judge whether it has reached the point at which action is needed; prevention, control, and follow-up should continue to be revised by new field information.
module.diagramTitle: Why Didn't He Miao Treat the Entire Bed as Soon as She Found Leaf Holes?
diagramSteps: Separate old leaf holes from fresh damage and record where new damage is concentrated
Continue identifying the insects present and confirm which observations are genuinely related to the current fresh damage
At the same time, tidy environmental conditions that complicate management, without treating housekeeping itself as proof of a pest source
Compare confirmed local pest activity and damage with the established action conditions; when action is warranted, compare suitable methods for effectiveness and risk before choosing targeted control
After control, continue checking for fresh damage and use the result to decide whether to maintain, adjust, or end the intervention
diagramStepNotes: A single leaf hole does not show that the entire crop is experiencing the same current pest problem; old and new damage need to be distinguished.
Seeing an insect does not mean the cause of the damage has been identified; identification needs to match the damage type, location, and continuing activity.
Prevention and environmental housekeeping are part of management, but without evidence a crate, corner, or facility should not be declared the pest source.
Action conditions depend on the specific crop, pest, stage, and health context; this example provides no universal number that can simply be reused.
Follow-up makes management a cycle: if damage continues, stops, or new information appears, the next action may change.
mapping: Old holes with dried edges → past damage that does not automatically mean the current problem is still expanding.
Continuing fresh feeding near the entrance → a current change requiring further investigation and monitoring.
Active pests confirmed as consistent with the fresh damage → the key information linking identification to the current injury.
The local area meeting pre-established action conditions → the decision point at which observation moves into targeted control.
Follow-up markers still present on Saturday → checking results after control rather than treating one intervention as the end of the process.
module.boundary: Integrated pest management does not mean always using less pesticide, never using pesticide, or always waiting first. Some situations may require rapid action, but whether to act and what form of control to use should depend on pest identity, crop and growth stage, progression of damage, health context, and an established professional plan. A single leaf hole, an unidentified insect, or one act of environmental housekeeping cannot substitute for that information. This story provides no real pesticide, dose, safety interval, harvesting permission, food-safety certification, or complete crop-protection program.
module.reflection: If the next inspection found the same number of old leaf holes but no fresh damage, while the previously confirmed pest activity had also disappeared, would you expect the manager to continue the same control or change the next decision first? Why?

references.citation: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. (2026, July 22, updated). Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Principles.
references.use: Supports an information-driven pest-management cycle built around action thresholds, monitoring and identification, prevention, multiple control methods, and checking results, and supports the reasonable use of control measures when needed. This article borrows only that decision framework, does not present any fictional field event as an EPA case, and provides no universal threshold, specific pesticide, dose, or globally applicable operating rule.

articles.summaryZh: 奶牛育种组下一阶段只够评估一个候选。程知眼前，生产预测最高的一份资料，并没有在每一列都领先。
storyParagraphsZh: 奶牛育种组的下一阶段预算被压缩，只够继续评估一个候选公牛资料。程知要在当天把名单交给负责人。候选A的生产性状遗传预测是+3，候选B只有+1；如果育种目标只看这一项，A显然更占优势。
可这轮筛选从一开始就不只关心生产。团队希望未来群体既保持生产改进，也不要把繁殖方向完全丢在一边，因此早在看到这两个候选前，就把本轮纸面目标写成“P+2F”。程知展开第二列：A的繁殖性状遗传预测是-1，B是+1。按同一个目标计算，A得到3+2×(-1)=1，B得到1+2×1=3。
这让名额真正变得难选。把资源给B，意味着暂时放弃继续追踪A更高的生产遗传预期；把资源给A，则意味着在唯一名额上牺牲团队事先给繁殖性状留下的权重。程知把两个候选的资料并排摊开，又看了一遍最初的目标页。
他最后把下一阶段评估名额留给B，同时把A完整保留在候选档案里。负责人来收名单，程知把写着“P+2F”的目标页也夹了进去，又在A的档案上记下暂缓评估的日期。
下午，资料管理员来收下一阶段文件。程知把B的资料装进唯一一个蓝色文件夹，把A夹回档案盒。关上盒盖前，他又看了一眼A那一列+3；那个单项优势仍然存在，只是没有拿到这一次唯一的评估名额。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：选择育种可以同时面对多个遗传目标，单项预测最高的候选不一定最符合预先定义的多性状目标；比较必须建立在可比的遗传评价和明确权重上。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本教学比较假设A和B属于同一品种、使用同一遗传评价基准，可靠性可比；生产P与繁殖F都已经标准化并统一成“越高越有利”的虚构遗传预测分。
教学目标P+2F在看到候选前已经确定，因此A=3+2×(-1)=1，B=1+2×1=3。这里不能把真实产奶公斤、繁殖天数等原始数值直接照加；真实多性状指数可通过合适系数处理单位和目标方向，还需考虑评价可靠性。
遗传评价描述的是对可遗传差异和未来群体表现方向的预测，不保证每个后代都实现同样结果。真实表型还受饲料、环境、年龄和管理等影响。两个候选在本例中出现的生产—繁殖权衡，也不能证明所有群体、所有性状之间都存在普遍负相关或必须互相牺牲。

moduleZh.intro: 先明确育种目标，再只比较处于同一评价基准、尺度和可靠性条件下的多项遗传预测；单项最高分不能自动替代综合目标。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么生产预测最高的A，没有得到唯一的下一阶段评估名额
diagramSteps: 固定本轮目标：同时考虑生产P与繁殖F，并在看到候选前确定教学权重P+2F
确认A、B来自同品种、同评价基准，P和F均已标准化为越高越有利且可靠性可比的预测分
记录候选A为P=+3、F=-1，候选B为P=+1、F=+1
把唯一下一阶段评估名额给综合目标得分更高的B，同时保留A较高生产预测这一机会成本
diagramStepNotes: 权重代表预先定义的育种目标；若目标改变，排序也可能改变。
本例简化为同品种、同基准、可靠性可比且已统一方向与尺度的分数。真实指数需由系数处理不同单位与目标方向，并考虑评价可靠性，不能把原始数字照此直接相加。
这些数值是虚构标准化遗传预测，不是牛奶公斤、繁殖天数、货币收益或真实PTA。
A=1、B=3只说明在这个特定教学目标下的综合排序，不说明B在每一个性状上都优于A。
选择B意味着放弃本轮继续追踪A更高生产预测的机会；多性状选择本身就是在目标之间配置有限选择压力。
mapping: A的P=+3 → 较高的生产性状遗传预期。
A的F=-1 → 在本例统一方向下较不利的繁殖性状遗传预期。
B的P=+1、F=+1 → 单项生产不及A，但两项目标方向更均衡。
P+2F → 事先确定的教学育种目标，而不是看到候选后临时修改的公式。
唯一评估名额 → 让多性状取舍产生实际机会成本的有限资源。
moduleZh.boundary: 本例中的+3、-1、+1和综合得分1、3均为虚构标准化遗传预测分，不是现实PTA、产奶量、繁殖天数或经济指数。只有在同品种、同评价基准、方向与尺度已统一且可靠性可比时，才有本例这种教学比较意义。选择育种改变的是未来群体的遗传预期，不保证每个后代的实际表现；环境、饲料、年龄与管理仍会影响表型。本例也不证明生产与繁殖性状在所有群体中普遍负相关，不提供现实配种或亲本选择处方。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果同样的两个候选被放进一个只重视生产、而不再给繁殖性状额外权重的育种目标中，你会预期排序可能怎样改变？这说明排序依赖什么？

referencesZh.citation: Armstrong, J., & Heins, B. (2023, reviewed). Dairy cattle genetics. University of Minnesota Extension.
referencesZh.use: 支持奶牛遗传评价和PTA属于预测、应在适当品种与评价基准内比较并考虑可靠性，也支持用多性状指数按育种目标赋权而不是只凭一个性状选择亲本；本篇只借用这些一般遗传评价关系，所有候选与标准分均为虚构，不使用真实PTA，也不提供现实配种方案。

articles.title: Only One Evaluation Slot Remained
articles.summary: The dairy breeding team can evaluate only one candidate in the next stage. The record with the highest production prediction does not lead in every column.
storyParagraphs: The dairy breeding team's budget for the next stage has been reduced, leaving enough resources to continue evaluating only one candidate bull record. Cheng Zhi has to submit the name that day. Candidate A has a production-trait genetic prediction of +3, while candidate B has only +1; if the breeding objective considered production alone, A would clearly have the advantage.

But this round of screening was never intended to focus on production alone. The team wants the future population to continue improving production without abandoning the fertility direction altogether, so before seeing these two candidates it had already defined the paper objective for this round as 'P+2F.' Cheng Zhi opens the second column: A's fertility-trait genetic prediction is -1, while B's is +1. Under the same objective, A scores 3+2×(-1)=1, while B scores 1+2×1=3.

That makes the single slot genuinely difficult. Giving the resources to B means temporarily giving up further evaluation of A's higher production genetic expectation; giving the resources to A means using the only slot while sacrificing the weight the team had deliberately assigned to fertility. Cheng Zhi lays the two candidate records side by side and looks again at the original objective sheet.

He gives the next-stage evaluation slot to B and keeps A's full record in the candidate archive. When the team leader comes for the list, Cheng Zhi includes the objective sheet marked “P+2F” and writes the date of the deferred evaluation on A's file.

That afternoon, the records administrator comes to collect the next-stage file. Cheng Zhi places B's material in the only blue folder and returns A's sheet to the archive box. Before closing the lid, he glances once more at A's +3 column. The single-trait advantage is still there; it simply did not receive the only evaluation slot available this time.
articles.overall: This article explains that selective breeding can involve several genetic objectives at the same time. The candidate with the highest single-trait prediction is not necessarily the best fit for a pre-defined multi-trait objective, and the comparison requires genetic evaluations that are genuinely comparable and weights that are clearly specified.
explanationParagraphs: This teaching comparison assumes that A and B belong to the same breed, use the same genetic-evaluation reference base, and have comparable reliability. Production P and fertility F have both been standardized and oriented so that higher values are favorable.

The teaching objective P+2F was fixed before the candidates were viewed, so A=3+2×(-1)=1 and B=1+2×1=3. Real milk kilograms, fertility days, or other raw trait values cannot simply be added as shown here. A real multi-trait index can use appropriate coefficients to account for units and goal directions, while evaluation reliability also needs consideration.

Genetic evaluation describes predictions about heritable differences and the expected direction of future population performance; it does not guarantee that every descendant will achieve the same result. Actual phenotype is also affected by feed, environment, age, management, and other factors. The production-fertility trade-off shown by these two candidates also does not prove that all populations or all traits have a universal negative genetic relationship or must always be sacrificed against one another.

module.intro: Define the breeding objective first, then compare multiple genetic predictions only when they share an appropriate evaluation base, scale, direction, and reliability context; the highest single-trait score cannot automatically replace the overall objective.
module.diagramTitle: Why Didn't A, with the Highest Production Prediction, Receive the Only Next-Stage Evaluation Slot?
diagramSteps: Fix the objective for this round: consider both production P and fertility F, with the teaching weight P+2F defined before viewing the candidates
Confirm that A and B are from the same breed and evaluation base, with P and F standardized so that higher is favorable and reliability is comparable
Record candidate A as P=+3 and F=-1, and candidate B as P=+1 and F=+1
Apply the pre-established objective to calculate A=3+2×(-1)=1 and B=1+2×1=3
Give the only next-stage evaluation slot to B, whose combined score better fits the objective, while retaining A's higher production prediction as the opportunity cost
diagramStepNotes: The weights represent the pre-defined breeding objective; if the objective changes, the ranking may also change.

This example simplifies the comparison to one breed and base, comparable reliability, and scores with a common scale and favorable direction. Real index coefficients must account for trait units and directions, and evaluation reliability needs consideration; raw values cannot simply be added as shown here.
These values are fictional standardized genetic predictions, not milk kilograms, fertility days, monetary returns, or real PTA values.
A=1 and B=3 describe only the ranking under this particular teaching objective; they do not mean B is superior to A in every trait.
Choosing B means giving up the opportunity to continue pursuing A's higher production prediction in this round; multi-trait selection allocates limited selection emphasis across objectives.
mapping: A's P=+3 → the higher genetic expectation for the production trait.
A's F=-1 → the less favorable fertility-trait genetic expectation under the common favorable direction used in this example.
B's P=+1 and F=+1 → lower production prediction than A but a more balanced direction across the two objectives.
P+2F → the pre-established teaching breeding objective, not a formula rewritten after the candidates were seen.
The single evaluation slot → the limited resource that turns the multi-trait comparison into a real opportunity-cost decision.
module.boundary: The values +3, -1, +1, and the combined scores 1 and 3 in this example are fictional standardized genetic prediction scores, not real PTA values, milk yield, fertility days, or an economic index. This kind of teaching comparison is meaningful only when candidates are from the same breed and evaluation base, trait directions and scales have been standardized, and reliability is comparable. Selective breeding changes expectations for the genetic direction of future populations; it does not guarantee the actual performance of every descendant, and environment, feed, age, and management still affect phenotype. This example also does not prove that production and fertility traits are universally negatively correlated and provides no real mating or parent-selection prescription.
module.reflection: If the same two candidates were placed under a breeding objective that valued production alone and no longer gave extra weight to fertility, how might you expect the ranking to change? What does that reveal about what the ranking depends on?

references.citation: Armstrong, J., & Heins, B. (2023, reviewed). Dairy cattle genetics. University of Minnesota Extension.
references.use: Supports treating dairy genetic evaluations and PTA as predictions that should be compared within an appropriate breed and evaluation base while considering reliability, and supports using multi-trait indexes weighted according to breeding objectives rather than selecting parents from a single trait alone. This article borrows only those general genetic-evaluation relationships; all candidates and standardized scores are fictional, no real PTA values are used, and no real mating plan is provided.

articles.summaryZh: 繁殖展只差一张主照片就能送印。志愿者选中了最旺的新枝，顾遥却蹲下来寻找它的起点。
storyParagraphsZh: 社区苗圃下周要布置繁殖展，顾遥只差一张主照片就能把展牌送去印刷。她特意选了一株教学样本：嫁接口还看得清，上面的枝条挂着一张来源标签，根系一侧也留着另一张。拍摄当天，两边都冒出了新枝，偏偏接口下方那一根长得最高、最抢镜。
志愿者已经蹲下来找角度，镜头里只剩那根旺枝和一片新叶。“用这一张吧，看起来最像成功。”顾遥没有回答，伸手顺着那根枝条一直找到它的起点。枝条从接口下方长出来，旁边正是根系一侧的标签；接口上方那枚刚展开的芽则靠近另一张来源标签。
她让志愿者先别按快门，把花盆转了半圈。新的构图里，嫁接口留在画面中央，两张标签分别出现在上、下两侧，那根最高的新枝也没有被裁掉。顾遥原来准备好的标题只有一句“新枝已经长出来了”，现在却显得太含糊：读者如果只看高度，根本不知道照片里最旺的枝条来自接口哪一边。
印刷因此推迟了一天。顾遥把新选的照片发给宣传同事，又在观察记录上写下上方萌芽的位置和日期。宣传同事把原来那张特写从版面里撤下，换上接口和两张标签都在画面中的照片，重新调整了标题的位置。
第二天下午，志愿者把新版展牌样张拿来。画面里最高的枝条仍然很显眼，但视线往下就能落到接口，再分别找到上下两张标签。顾遥把样张靠在花盆边比了一下。志愿者这次没有问哪根长得最快，只指着接口上方那枚芽说：“我们等的是这里，对吧？”顾遥把样张收进文件袋：“先把它从哪里长出来说清楚。”
articles.overallZh: 本篇用一株带清楚嫁接口和来源标签的教学样本说明嫁接与繁殖的一个入口：嫁接把接穗的芽或枝连接到相容砧木上，接穗形成上部生长部分，砧木提供根系；两部分通过愈合建立维管联系后成为一个可共同生长的植株系统，但仍保留各自来源的遗传身份。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例中，嫁接口上方带有接穗来源标签，接口下方和根系一侧带有砧木来源标签，因此可以根据可见新枝从接口哪一侧萌出，判断这根枝条属于接穗还是砧木。接穗来自目标来源植株，并保留其来源品种的遗传身份；砧木保留自己的遗传身份并提供根系，也可能影响树势等整株表现。嫁接把两个部分连接起来，并不是像种子杂交那样把它们混成一个新的杂交遗传身份。
嫁接要让相容、健康的两部分愈合，形成能输送水分和养分的组织连接，也就是维管联系。Texas A&M指出，接穗有时会在连接尚未建立时先萌芽。萌芽、愈伤组织和持续生长都可作为观察线索，但一张外观照片不足以确认内部连接及其长期稳定；砧木萌蘖也不能作为接穗生长的证据。本例只用接口位置和已知来源标签判断新枝来源，长期连接仍需后续观察。

moduleZh.intro: 先用嫁接口位置和来源标签判断可见新枝来自接穗还是砧木，再把枝条来源与嫁接连接是否长期建立分开判断。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么最高的新枝不能自动代表上部接穗已经成功生长
diagramSteps: 确认教学样本具有清楚的嫁接口以及上部接穗、下部砧木两个来源标签
沿最高新枝回查其萌出位置，发现它来自嫁接口下方的砧木一侧
观察接口上方另有一枚来自接穗一侧的新芽，并在照片中同时保留接口和两张标签
用来源位置区分接穗上部与砧木根部的作用，同时说明两者保持各自遗传身份
把早期萌芽与长期嫁接成功分开，后续仍需观察愈合、维管连接和持续生长
diagramStepNotes: 枝条高度、叶色或长势本身不能替代接口位置与来源记录。
接口下方的新枝属于砧木一侧，不能用作接穗已经旺盛生长的证据。
接口上方萌芽可以帮助判断可见枝条来源，但萌芽本身还不能证明内部连接已经长期建立。
接穗通常保留来源植株的遗传身份，砧木也保留自身身份；嫁接不是种子杂交。
有效长期连接涉及相容性、健康、愈合和维管连续，照片或外观不能单独完成这一判断。
mapping: 接口上方来源标签 → 接穗一侧及其来源身份。
接口下方根系标签 → 砧木一侧及其来源身份。
最高的新枝 → 从砧木一侧萌出的可见枝条，不代表接穗长势。
接口上方的新芽 → 来自接穗一侧的可见新生长，但不等于长期连接已确认。
主照片同时保留接口和两张标签 → 让观众先判断枝条来源，而不是只按外观猜测。
moduleZh.boundary: 并非所有植物或所有接穗—砧木组合都能成功嫁接。长期成功需要相容性、健康材料、适当愈合并形成有效维管联系；早期萌芽、叶片展开、愈伤外观或照片都不能单独证明这一点。砧木可以影响树势等表现，因此也不能宣称嫁接后整株所有性状都只是接穗的简单复制，或果味、大小等一定不变。本篇不提供刀口尺寸、操作温湿度、时长、成活率、病害管理步骤或现实嫁接操作指导。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果新芽确定长在嫁接口上方，你已经能判断什么，又还不能据此判断什么？要讨论长期嫁接成功，还需要观察哪些变化？

referencesZh.use: 支持接穗形成植株上部、砧木提供根系，以及亲和性、形成层接触、健康与愈合对嫁接的重要性；同时支持嫁接通常不把接穗与砧木混成种子杂交产生的新遗传品种。本篇不据此保证所有组合成活、接口长期稳定或果实性状完全不变。

referencesZh.use: 支持接穗作为来源植株的遗传复制部分、愈合组织进一步形成维管连接，以及接穗可能在嫁接连接尚未建立时先出现萌芽、砧木自身也可能萌蘖；本篇只借用这些形态、连接和判断边界，不采用来源中的刀口、温湿度、时间或成活率作为操作建议，也不凭照片确认内部维管连续。

articles.title: The Tallest Shoot in the Photograph
articles.summary: The propagation exhibit needs one main photograph before it can go to print. A volunteer picks the most vigorous new shoot, while Gu Yao crouches down to trace its origin.
storyParagraphs: The community nursery is setting up a propagation exhibit the following week, and Gu Yao needs only one main photograph before the display panel can go to print. She deliberately chooses a teaching specimen on which the graft union is still clearly visible, with one source label attached to the upper shoot and another retained on the root side. On the day of the photo shoot, new growth has appeared on both sides, and the shoot below the union happens to be the tallest and most eye-catching.

The volunteer has already crouched down to find an angle, leaving only the vigorous shoot and one new leaf in the frame. “Let's use this one. It looks most like success.” Gu Yao does not answer. She follows the shoot all the way back to its point of origin. It emerges below the graft union, beside the label on the root side; the newly opening bud above the union sits near the other source label.

She asks the volunteer not to press the shutter yet and turns the pot halfway around. In the new composition, the graft union remains in the centre, the two labels appear above and below it, and the tallest new shoot is still visible rather than being cropped out. Gu Yao's original title had only said, “New growth has appeared.” Now it feels too vague: if readers look only at height, they have no way to know which side of the union produced the most vigorous shoot in the photograph.

Printing is delayed by one day. Gu Yao sends the new photograph to the communications colleague and adds the position and date of the upper bud to the observation record. The colleague removes the original close-up from the layout, replaces it with the image showing the union and both labels, and adjusts the title’s position.

The next afternoon, the volunteer brings over the revised display proof. The tallest shoot is still conspicuous in the image, but following it downward leads the eye to the union and then to the two labels above and below. Gu Yao holds the proof beside the pot. This time the volunteer does not ask which shoot is growing fastest. Instead, he points to the bud above the union. “This is the one we're waiting for, right?” Gu Yao slips the proof into the document pouch. “First make clear where it came from.”
articles.overall: This article uses a teaching specimen with a clearly visible graft union and source labels to introduce one aspect of grafting and propagation: grafting connects a bud or shoot from a scion to a compatible rootstock. The scion forms the upper growth, while the rootstock provides the root system. After healing establishes vascular continuity, the two parts function together as one growing plant system while retaining the genetic identity of their respective sources.
explanationParagraphs: In this example, the area above the graft union carries the scion-source label, while the area below the union and the root side carries the rootstock-source label. The visible point from which a shoot emerges can therefore be used to determine whether that shoot belongs to the scion or the rootstock. The scion comes from the target source plant and retains the genetic identity of that source variety. The rootstock retains its own genetic identity and provides the root system, while also potentially influencing traits such as plant vigour. Grafting connects the two parts; it does not combine them into a new hybrid genetic identity in the way seed hybridization can.

Grafting requires compatible, healthy parts to heal and form connected tissues that transport water and nutrients: a vascular connection. Texas A&M notes that a scion may sprout before a graft connection is established. Bud emergence, callus tissue and sustained growth can provide useful observations, but one outward photograph cannot establish the internal connection or its long-term stability. A rootstock shoot is also not evidence of scion growth. This example uses the union position and known source labels only to identify new-shoot origin; a lasting connection still requires further observation.

module.intro: First use the graft-union position and source labels to determine whether a visible shoot comes from the scion or the rootstock, then keep shoot origin separate from whether a durable graft connection has been established.
module.diagramTitle: Why Doesn't the Tallest New Shoot Automatically Show That the Upper Scion Has Successfully Established?
diagramSteps: Confirm that the teaching specimen has a clear graft union and separate source labels for the upper scion and lower rootstock
Trace the tallest new shoot back to its point of emergence and find that it comes from the rootstock side below the graft union
Observe a separate bud above the union on the scion side and keep the union and both labels visible in the photograph
Use the source positions to distinguish the roles of the upper scion and the rootstock while recognizing that each retains its own genetic identity
Keep early bud emergence separate from long-term graft success and continue observing healing, vascular connection, and sustained growth
diagramStepNotes: Shoot height, leaf colour, or apparent vigour cannot substitute for graft-union position and source records.
A new shoot below the union belongs to the rootstock side and cannot serve as evidence that the scion is growing strongly.
A bud above the union can help identify visible growth as coming from the scion side, but bud emergence alone does not prove that an internal connection has been durably established.
The scion normally retains the genetic identity of its source plant, and the rootstock retains its own identity; grafting is not seed hybridization.
A durable functional connection involves compatibility, health, healing, and vascular continuity, none of which can be fully established from a photograph or outward appearance alone.
mapping: Source label above the union → the scion side and its source identity.
Root-side label below the union → the rootstock side and its source identity.
Tallest new shoot → a visible shoot emerging from the rootstock side, not evidence of scion growth.
New bud above the union → visible new growth from the scion side, but not confirmation of a durable connection.
Main photograph showing the union and both labels → lets viewers first determine shoot origin instead of guessing from appearance alone.
module.boundary: Not all plants or all scion-rootstock combinations can be grafted successfully. Long-term success requires compatibility, healthy material, appropriate healing, and the formation of an effective vascular connection. Early bud emergence, leaf expansion, the appearance of callus, or a photograph cannot by themselves prove that this has occurred. Rootstocks can also influence characteristics such as vigour, so grafting does not mean that every whole-plant trait is simply copied from the scion or that fruit flavour, size, or other traits must remain unchanged. This article provides no cut dimensions, temperature or humidity settings, timing, success rates, disease-management steps, or real-world grafting instructions.
module.reflection: If a new bud definitely emerges above the graft union, what can you now identify, and what can you still not conclude from that alone? What further changes would you observe before discussing long-term graft success?

references.citation: University of Missouri Extension. (2022, August). Grafting (G6971), reviewed by David Trinklein.
references.use: Supports that the scion forms the upper part of the plant, the rootstock provides the root system, and compatibility, cambial contact, health, and healing are important to grafting. It also supports that grafting generally does not combine scion and rootstock into a new genetic variety in the manner of seed hybridization. This article does not use the source to guarantee that all combinations survive, that graft unions remain stable long term, or that fruit traits remain completely unchanged.

references.citation: Hartmann, T. (2020, May). Whip and Tongue Grafting (HORT-PU-169). Texas A&M AgriLife Extension.
references.use: Supports the scion as a genetic copy of the source plant, healing tissue developing into a vascular connection, the possibility that a scion may begin to bud before a graft connection has been established, and the possibility of rootstock suckering. This article borrows only those morphological, connection, and judgment boundaries, does not use the source's cut dimensions, temperature, humidity, timing, or success rates as operating advice, and does not claim that a photograph can confirm internal vascular continuity.

articles.summaryZh: 植物展原本要在小院入口做对称陈列。第一次试摆到下午，林初发现相隔几步的两组盆栽并不一样。
storyParagraphsZh: 周末植物展要占用一座不大的内院，林初想让入口两边各摆一组盆栽，进门就能看到整齐的对称效果。地区天气预报并没有显示什么异常，她以为两个位置相隔不过几步，差别不会太大。第一次试摆到下午，靠玻璃墙的一组却先显得疲软。
她没有马上给这个现象找一个单一原因。第二天，林初从同一批展示植物里挑出两组原本就使用相同规格容器、同批基质并有相近日常浇水记录的盆栽，再放回两个位置。她要看的不是哪一株为什么萎蔫，而是这两个位置在展览时段里会不会反复呈现不同条件。
接下来几个时段里，位置差异一次次出现。玻璃墙一侧下午受直射光更久，同时风感较弱；入口转角一侧较早进入建筑阴影，空气流动也更明显。两边盆面的干燥节奏也常常不同。林初没有把这些现象压成一个单独原因，只在平面图上分别记下阳光、阴影、风和盆面状态什么时候出现变化。
原来的对称方案因此被她拆开。主入口展示组被调整到下午较早进入阴影的那一侧，玻璃墙旁减少盆数，并留出工作人员查看的通道。入口失去了左右完全对称的效果，工作人员也多了一段巡查路线。林初把这段绕行画到展期值班表上，交给接班的同事。
开展第一天下午，玻璃墙的亮边慢慢爬过地砖，停在原先准备放第二排盆栽的位置。林初低头看了一眼记录板上的时间，在那一格画上短线，又把旁边一只备用展盆移到新布置图标出的空位。旧的对称布置图还压在板夹最下面。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：同一个地区天气背景下，相隔很近的位置仍可能因为建筑、遮阴和气流等条件形成不同的局部环境，植物实际经历的光、水热和风并不一定相同。
explanationParagraphsZh: 地区天气与院子里的局部差异可以同时正确。建筑墙面、遮阴时序、地面和周围植被会改变局部受光与热交换，墙角、开口和障碍物会改变气流；这些因素又会与盆体和水分交换一起影响植物实际经历的环境。因此相隔几步的位置也可能在同一时段出现不同条件。
例如，建筑遮阴会在遮挡时段减少到达盆栽的直射太阳辐射，从而改变热量输入；这能解释位置条件为何不同，却不能单凭这一点确定某株萎蔫的原因。
本故事的重复观察只支持‘这些展览时段里两个位置的环境条件反复不同’，不能证明某次萎蔫只有一个原因，也不能推出四季永久保持同样差异。光照更久和风更弱同时出现，也不能单独把任何一项宣布为全部变化的原因；盆栽初始状态、根部、水分历史等仍可能影响表现。

moduleZh.intro: 把地区天气作为大背景，再观察建筑、遮阴和气流如何让相邻位置形成不同的局部条件；重复位置差异比一次植物反应更能支持摆位判断。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么同一个小院、同一天气下，两组相邻盆栽仍可能经历不同环境
diagramSteps: 从同一批植物中选择原本就较可比的匹配盆栽，分别放到玻璃墙侧和入口转角侧
在多个展览时段重复记录两处何时受直射光、何时进入阴影以及空气流动是否明显
同时观察两处盆面状态的变化节奏，但不把它单独当成某种病因或水分诊断
发现玻璃墙侧在这些时段反复受光更久且风较弱，转角侧较早遮阴且空气流动更明显
据此调整展盆数量、主入口展示位置和巡查路线，同时继续把该安排视为特定展期条件下的选择
diagramStepNotes: 使用原本就较匹配的盆栽是为了减少明显初始差异，不等于排除了所有植物个体差异。
重复观察支持的是位置条件差异，不是用一次萎蔫确认单一因果。
盆面变化会受光、风、容器、基质、植株和水分历史等多项因素影响。
光照更久与风较弱在故事中同时出现，不能分别宣称任何一项单独造成全部植物反应。
展期摆位可以随季节、天气和现场变化重新评估，不是永久园区分区规则。
mapping: 玻璃墙一侧 → 在本次展览观察时段内受直射光较久、风感较弱的位置。
入口转角一侧 → 较早进入建筑阴影且空气流动更明显的位置。
地区天气预报 → 描述较大尺度天气背景，并不否定院内小尺度差异。
取消完全对称陈列 → 因局部条件不同而付出的空间与视觉代价。
记录板与巡查路线 → 用重复观察继续检查局部条件，而不是一次性永久定区。
moduleZh.boundary: 微气候描述的是比地区天气尺度更小的局部环境差异，不意味着附近天气站错误。建筑、地形、遮阴、地面、植被和气流都可能改变植物经历的光照、热交换和水分条件，但一次萎蔫、一次盆面干燥或单一位置观察都不能排除根部、浇水、基质或初始植株差异。地域朝向经验也不能无条件推广到全球。本篇不提供防霜、灌溉、病害诊断、永久分区或园艺工程参数。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果同一个展区换到另一个季节，太阳路径和盛行风方向都发生变化，你会继续沿用这次的摆位，还是重新观察两个位置？这说明微气候判断为什么需要时间和情境？

referencesZh.citation: Royal Meteorological Society. (2017, July 28). Microclimates in the garden.
referencesZh.use: 支持小尺度园地内部可以出现光照、风、温度和湿度差异，并支持地形、朝向、墙体、篱障和容器等改变局部环境；本篇不搬用来源中的具体温差或降雨比例，也不把某一地域朝向经验推广成全球规律。

referencesZh.citation: Royal Horticultural Society Advice Team. (n.d.). Microclimates: assessing your garden.
referencesZh.use: 支持地区气候背景与园内小尺度差异并存，并支持通过建筑、遮阴、风口、地形和季节变化观察局部条件；本篇只借用位置评估逻辑，不提供现实防霜、灌溉参数、病害诊断或合规设计。

articles.title: Two Sides of the Courtyard
articles.summary: The plant exhibition is meant to have a symmetrical courtyard entrance. By the afternoon of the first trial, Lin Chu notices a difference between two groups of pots just a few steps apart.
storyParagraphs: A weekend plant exhibition will occupy a small courtyard, and Lin Chu wants to place one group of potted plants on each side of the entrance for a clean symmetrical view. The regional weather forecast shows nothing unusual, and she assumes that two spots only a few steps apart will not differ much. By the afternoon of the first trial arrangement, however, the group beside the glass wall looks tired first.

She does not immediately assign a single cause to the observation. The next day, Lin Chu selects two groups from the same batch of display plants that already use containers of the same specification, the same batch of growing medium, and have similar routine watering records, and places them back in the two positions. What she wants to see is not why one particular plant wilted, but whether the two locations repeatedly present different conditions during the exhibition period.

Over the next several observation periods, the location differences recur. The glass-wall side receives direct afternoon sunlight for longer and at the same time feels less windy; the entrance-corner side enters building shade earlier and has more noticeable air movement. The drying pattern at the pot surface also often differs between the two sides. Lin Chu does not compress these observations into a single cause. On the floor plan, she separately records when sunlight and shade shift, when airflow is more noticeable, and when the pot surfaces change.

She breaks up the original symmetrical arrangement. The main entrance display group moves to the side that enters shade earlier in the afternoon. Beside the glass wall, she reduces the number of pots and leaves a passage for staff to inspect them. The entrance loses its perfect symmetry, and staff have a longer inspection route. Lin Chu marks the extra loop on the exhibition duty sheet and hands it to the colleague taking the next shift.

On the first afternoon of the exhibition, the edge of the sunlit patch beside the glass wall slowly moves across the paving and stops at the place where the second row of pots had originally been planned. Lin Chu glances at the time on her record board, marks that box with a short line, and moves a nearby spare display pot into the empty position shown on the revised layout. The old symmetrical plan remains underneath the clipboard.
articles.overall: This article explains that under the same regional weather background, nearby locations can still develop different local environmental conditions because of buildings, shade, and airflow, so plants may not experience the same light, heat-and-water conditions, or wind even when they are only a few steps apart.
explanationParagraphs: Regional weather and local differences within a courtyard can both be correct. Building surfaces, the timing of shade, the ground, and surrounding vegetation can alter local exposure to light and heat exchange, while corners, openings, and obstacles can alter airflow. These factors also interact with containers and water exchange to shape the environment plants actually experience. Locations only a few steps apart can therefore differ during the same period.

For example, building shade reduces the direct solar radiation reaching a pot while it is shaded, changing the heat input. That explains one way locations can differ, without establishing the cause of a particular plant's wilting.

The repeated observations in this story support only the conclusion that the two locations repeatedly differed during these exhibition periods. They do not prove that a particular episode of wilting had a single cause, nor do they show that the same differences will persist unchanged through every season. Longer sunlight exposure and weaker airflow also occurred together, so neither one can be declared by itself to explain all of the observed changes; initial plant condition, roots, watering history, and other factors may still affect plant response.

module.intro: Treat regional weather as the broader background, then observe how buildings, shade, and airflow create different local conditions at nearby positions; repeated location differences support placement decisions more strongly than a single plant response does.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can Two Nearby Groups of Potted Plants Experience Different Conditions in the Same Courtyard and the Same Weather?
diagramSteps: Select already comparable groups of potted plants from the same batch and place them at the glass-wall side and the entrance-corner side
Across several exhibition periods, repeatedly record when each location receives direct sunlight, when it enters shade, and whether airflow is noticeable
At the same time, observe the pattern of change at the pot surface without using it alone as a diagnosis of water status or disease
Observe that during these periods the glass-wall side repeatedly receives longer sunlight and weaker airflow, while the corner side enters shade earlier and has more noticeable air movement

Use those repeated location differences to adjust pot numbers, the main entrance display position, and the inspection route, while treating the arrangement as a choice for this particular exhibition period
diagramStepNotes: Using plants that were already relatively well matched reduces obvious initial differences but does not eliminate all individual plant variation.
Repeated observation supports a difference between locations; it does not use one episode of wilting to prove a single cause.
Pot-surface change can be influenced by light, airflow, the container, growing medium, the plant, and watering history.
Longer sunlight and weaker airflow occur together in the story, so neither can be claimed separately to cause the entire plant response.
The exhibition layout can be reassessed as season, weather, and site conditions change; it is not a permanent zoning rule for the garden.
mapping: Glass-wall side → a location that, during the observed exhibition periods, receives direct sunlight for longer and has weaker perceived airflow.
Entrance-corner side → a location that enters building shade earlier and has more noticeable air movement.
Regional weather forecast → the broader-scale weather background, which does not rule out small-scale differences within the courtyard.
Giving up perfect symmetry → the spatial and visual trade-off made because local conditions differ.
Record board and inspection route → continued repeated observation of local conditions rather than a one-time permanent classification.
module.boundary: Microclimate describes local environmental differences at a smaller scale than regional weather and does not imply that a nearby weather station is wrong. Buildings, topography, shade, ground surfaces, vegetation, and airflow can all change the light, heat exchange, and water conditions experienced by plants, but one episode of wilting, one instance of a dry pot surface, or one location observation cannot exclude root conditions, watering, growing medium, or initial plant differences. Rules of thumb about orientation are also not universally transferable across regions. This article provides no frost-protection parameters, irrigation settings, disease diagnosis, permanent zoning rule, or horticultural engineering specification.
module.reflection: If the same exhibition area were used in another season and both the sun path and prevailing wind direction had changed, would you keep the same placement or observe the two positions again? What does that suggest about why microclimate judgments depend on time and context?

references.citation: Royal Meteorological Society. (2017, July 28). Microclimates in the garden.
references.use: Supports the existence of small-scale differences in light, wind, temperature, and humidity within a garden and supports that topography, orientation, walls, hedges, and containers can modify local conditions. This article does not reuse the source's specific temperature differences or rainfall proportions and does not generalize any region-specific orientation rule into a global rule.

references.citation: Royal Horticultural Society Advice Team. (n.d.). Microclimates: assessing your garden.
references.use: Supports that regional climate and small-scale variation within a garden can coexist and supports observing buildings, shade, wind exposure, topography, and seasonal change when assessing local conditions. This article borrows only that location-assessment logic and provides no real frost-protection method, irrigation parameter, disease diagnosis, or compliant design.

articles.title: The Calendar Was Not Late
articles.summary: The orchard receives its hives on the same date every year; when blossom opens early, the bees arrive exactly on time beneath falling petals.
articles.summaryZh: 果园每年都在同一天迎接蜂箱，那年梨花提前开放，蜂车准时到达时，枝头已经落满白瓣。
storyParagraphs: White Creek Orchard followed a calendar left by the owner's grandfather: hives arrived on 12 April, flowers were thinned on 20 April, and late-frost precautions began in early May. For decades the dates rarely failed. Owner He Jia printed them on the shed wall so no one needed to look up and guess the season. Fixed bookings reduced coordination cost and had worked long enough to become invisible infrastructure.

One winter was unusually warm, followed by clear heat at the end of February. Pear branches filled with blossom before March ended, but the beekeeper arrived on the contracted 12 April. The hive cart entered exactly on time as white petals covered the ground. A later frost then damaged the early fruit, and autumn yield was less than half the usual crop. The hive rental and lost crop consumed the reserve intended for irrigation repairs.
He let the old contract expire and paid to build field observations into the next decision.

The delay cost him an early-booking discount. He trained workers to record standard stages rather than impressions such as 'spring feels early.' Dates, temperature accumulation, variety, and observer were kept together. Workers compared first bloom, peak bloom, and fruit set across varieties; a single early flower no longer triggered the whole plan.

He blamed the beekeeper for arriving late; the beekeeper pointed to the date in the contract. A naturalist opened years of records. Pear bloom responded to winter chilling, later warmth, and variety. Wild bees and other insects could follow different cues, while frost did not necessarily move earlier with flowering. The calendar had not been late, but dependent living events had moved apart. Degree-day models were treated as aids and recalibrated with observations, while frost risk remained a separate forecast and contingency.

The orchard began weekly standardized records of bud swelling, first and peak bloom, insect appearance, and frost dates, preserving long comparisons. Hive movement followed buds and short-term forecasts rather than the month alone. Early and late flowering resources remained at the orchard edge, reducing reliance on one delivery. Records improved prediction without removing uncertainty among varieties, sites, and years. Historical records were not discarded; they became a baseline against which shifts and mismatches could be tested. The second hive delivery was split into two windows, costing more transport but reducing dependence on one predicted date.

When the first pear flower opened the following March, He took down the old calendar. He drew a thin line through 12 April and wrote the current date in the first box of the flowering record. The erased date stayed readable.
storyParagraphsZh: 白溪果园沿用祖父留下的日历：四月十二日运来蜂箱，四月二十日疏花，五月初防晚霜。几十年里，这套日期很少出错。园主何嘉把安排印在工棚墙上，谁也不必再抬头猜季节。固定日期降低协调成本，又连续多年有效，久而久之便像无需检查的基础设施。
一个冬天异常温暖，二月末又连续晴热。梨花在三月底便开满枝头，可蜂农仍按合同在四月十二日抵达。蜂车准时驶进果园时，地上已经铺着白瓣。随后一场晚霜又伤了过早萌出的幼果，秋天收成不到往年一半。蜂箱租金和歉收耗掉原本维修灌溉的储备。
何嘉眼看旧供货合同到期，付钱把田间观察写进下一轮决策。
这次拖延让他失去提前预订折扣。他训练工人记录统一阶段，不再写“春天似乎早”。日期、积温、品种与观察者一起保存。工人按品种比较初花、盛花与坐果，不再由一朵早花启动全部安排。
何嘉责怪蜂农来迟，蜂农指着合同上的日期。自然观察员却翻出多年记录：梨树开花受低温积累、后续热量和品种影响，野蜂与昆虫还可能依赖不同线索，霜冻也不会随花期一起前移。日历没有迟到，彼此依赖的生命事件却已经错开。积温模型只作辅助，并用实测校准；霜冻风险仍有独立预报与预案。
果园开始每周记录芽膨大、初花、盛花、昆虫出现和霜日，并使用统一标准，保留长期比较。蜂箱调运改看花芽与短期预报，不再只看月份；园边也保留早晚开花的资源，减少完全依赖一次到车。记录帮助预测，却不能消除品种、地点和年份的不确定。旧日历没有被丢弃，而成为检验变化与错配的基线。蜂箱分两批到场，多付运输费，却减少对一个预测日期的依赖。
第二年三月，第一朵梨花打开。何嘉取下墙上的旧日历，在四月十二日旁画了一条细线，又把当天日期写在花期记录的第一格。被划过的旧日期仍然可辨。
explanationParagraphs: Phenology studies the timing of recurring life events such as flowering, migration, breeding, and leaf fall and their relationship with seasonal and year-to-year environments. Different organisms may respond to chilling, accumulated warmth, day length, moisture, genetics, and other cues, so environmental change can create mismatches. Standardized long-term observations reveal trends, but prediction remains specific to organism, site, and context.
explanationParagraphsZh: 物候学研究开花、迁徙、繁殖、落叶等反复生命事件的时间，以及它们同季节和年际环境的关系。不同生物可能分别响应低温积累、热量、日长、水分和遗传等线索，因此环境变化会造成相互作用错配。标准化长期观察能揭示趋势，但预测必须针对物种、地点和情境。

articles.summaryZh: 木工坊想提前排好下一季的材料，许岑桌上的生长预测看起来也有余地。回复供料前，她又翻到了另一行记录。
storyParagraphsZh: 社区木工坊正在排下一季的长桌订单，想先把教学林地未来可能提供的木料锁进生产表。许岑负责给出下一管理期能不能继续按计划移除9个活立木体积单位的建议。她桌上的预测表显示，这一拟议期从100个活立木体积单位开始，预计毛生长12；第一眼看去，9似乎还留着余地。
她正准备回复木工坊，看到预测表下面还有一行预计自然死亡4。许岑把三项变化放到同一个拟议期里：毛生长12先扣自然死亡4，得到净增长8；如果再按计划采伐9个同口径的活立木体积单位，预测期末就是100+12-4-9=99。她在“12”旁边重新写上“毛生长”，免得它以后被误读成已经扣过死亡的净增长。
木工坊已经按整期供料安排好了加工时段。许岑打电话把原来的整期锁量改成分段确认：加工档期先保留，后段从这片林地实际能确认多少，再根据后续资源信息更新。负责人得重新安排配料，部分材料来源也可能需要调整。
同事问，预测期末只比期初少1个单位，是否值得动已经排好的安排。许岑把预测表推过去：“算完这一期的体积，还得看接下来由哪些树补上。更新、林木大小和年龄，还有这些预测有多稳，都要一起看。”她把更新和林分结构资料放到预留单旁边，准备核对后半段供料。
傍晚，木工坊把新的生产表发回来。原来横跨整季的一条供料预留被拆成前后两段，后半段留着待确认标记。许岑把它和预测表夹在一起。屏幕上，前半段的加工档期仍在原来的位置。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：判断可持续采伐不能只拿毛生长和计划采伐直接比较。必须在同一林地、时期和活立木体积口径下，把毛生长、死亡和采伐分开核算，再结合更新、林分结构与不确定性判断长期生产能力。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例固定同一片林地、同一个拟议管理期和同一活立木体积口径，不另计林地面积、分类变化或其他转入转出。期初100、预计毛生长12、预计自然死亡4，则净增长12-4=8；若计划采伐9，预测期末100+12-4-9=99。
12是毛生长；如果资料给出的已是净增长，就不能再减一次死亡。9也指计划移除的活立木体积，不是加工后成品量，本例没有给木料加工得率。
从100到99只是单期库存预测，不是现实许可或长期不可持续的证明。持续供给还需足够更新、合适林分结构及对未来生长和死亡的判断。死亡和采伐是不同流量，死木仍可能留在生态系统中发挥作用。

moduleZh.intro: 先固定同一林地、同一时期和同一活立木体积口径，再把毛生长、死亡和采伐分别放入库存变化，并把单期算术与长期生产能力分开。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么预计毛生长12，仍不能直接把9个单位的计划采伐视为长期可持续
diagramSteps: 固定拟议期初活立木体积为100单位，并确认所有变化都使用同一活立木体积口径
记录预计毛生长12单位，并确认这12尚未扣除自然死亡和采伐
扣除预计自然死亡4单位，得到本拟议期预计净增长8单位
再扣除计划采伐9单位，得到预测期末100+12-4-9=99单位
把99视为单期库存结果，再结合更新、林分结构和不确定性决定是否需要调整后续供给安排
diagramStepNotes: 如果林地边界、时间范围或活立木分类不同，数字不能直接放在同一库存账中比较。
毛生长与净增长不是同一个量；净增长若已经扣除死亡，就不能再次减死亡。
自然死亡与采伐必须分开记录；死亡木材不因此自动成为额外可采量。
计划采伐9指同一活立木体积口径下的计划移除量，不等于9单位加工后木料或成品产量。
预测期末99既不自动证明长期不可持续，也不证明长期可以维持固定采伐；长期判断还需要更新和结构信息。
mapping: 期初100 → 拟议期开始时同一固定林地内的活立木体积。
毛生长12 → 拟议期内预计新增的活立木体积，尚未扣死亡。
自然死亡4 → 从活立木库存中退出的预计死亡量，与采伐分开。
计划采伐9 → 同一活立木体积口径下拟议移除的量，不是加工成品量。
分段确认供料 → 把单期库存预测与更新、结构等后续信息连接到实际排程。
moduleZh.boundary: 本例中的100、12、4、9和99均为虚构教学预测，不是实测林业数据或现实采伐许可。可持续采伐量关注的是不削弱长期生产能力的持续供给，但单期库存持平或接近持平都不足以证明更新、生物多样性或林分结构良好。若输入数据是净增长而非毛生长，死亡不得重复扣除。枯死木在生态系统中仍可能具有其他作用，本篇也不提供现实清理、采伐或经营操作指导。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果新表上写的是“净增长8”，并已扣除自然死亡4，你会怎样计算计划采伐9后的存量？为什么不能再把4减一次？

referencesZh.citation: Goff, T. C., et al. (2022). Iowa forests 2018: summary report. Resource Bulletin NRS-128. USDA Forest Service, Northern Research Station.
referencesZh.use: 支持区分毛生长、死亡与净增长，并支持把持续生产能力与再生更新、林分结构等长期条件联系起来；本篇只借用这些森林清查口径与长期供给原则，不把100、12、4、9、99等虚构教学数字称为Iowa报告数据，也不据此给出现实采伐量。

articles.title: The Second Half of the Reservation
articles.summary: The workshop wants to plan next season’s materials, and the growth projection on Xu Cen’s desk seems to leave room. Before confirming supply, she notices another line.
storyParagraphs: The community woodworking shop is scheduling its next season of long-table orders and wants to lock into its production plan the timber that the teaching forest may be able to provide. Xu Cen is responsible for advising whether the next management period can still include the planned removal of 9 units of live-tree volume. The projection sheet on her desk shows that the proposed period begins with 100 units of live-tree volume and is expected to have gross growth of 12. At first glance, 9 seems to leave some room.

She is about to reply to the workshop when she notices another line on the projection sheet: projected natural mortality of 4. Xu Cen places the three changes within the same proposed period. Gross growth of 12 minus natural mortality of 4 gives net growth of 8; if 9 units of live-tree volume on the same accounting basis are then harvested as planned, the projected ending volume is 100+12-4-9=99. Beside the '12,' she writes 'gross growth' again so that it will not later be misread as net growth that already excludes mortality.

The woodworking shop has already scheduled processing time around the full-period supply arrangement. Xu Cen calls to change the original locked quantity to staged confirmation: the processing slot stays reserved, while the amount that can later be confirmed from this forest will be updated as further resource information arrives. The manager has to revise the material schedule and may need to adjust some material sources.

A colleague asks whether it is worth changing an established arrangement when the projected ending volume is only 1 unit below the opening volume. Xu Cen pushes the projection sheet across the desk. “After calculating this period’s volume, we still need to see which trees will replenish it. Regeneration, tree sizes and ages, and how reliable these projections are all matter.” She places the regeneration and stand-structure material beside the reservation form to check the later supply section.

That evening, the woodworking shop sends back the revised production sheet. The supply reservation that once stretched across the season has been split into an early and a later section, with the second marked pending confirmation. Xu Cen clips it to the projection sheet. On the screen, the earlier processing slot remains in its original place.
articles.overall: This article explains that sustainable-yield reasoning cannot simply compare gross growth with planned harvest. Gross growth, mortality, and harvest must be accounted for separately within the same forest area, time period, and live-tree-volume basis, and long-term productive capacity also depends on regeneration, stand structure, and uncertainty.
explanationParagraphs: This example fixes one forest area, proposed management period and live-tree-volume basis, with no additional area, classification or other transfers. Opening volume 100, projected gross growth 12 and projected mortality 4 give net growth 12-4=8. With planned harvest 9, projected ending volume is 100+12-4-9=99.

The 12 is gross growth. If the input already reports net growth, mortality must not be deducted again. The 9 is planned live-tree-volume removal, not finished-product output; no wood-processing conversion yield is given.

The movement from 100 to 99 is one inventory projection, not a permit or proof of long-term unsustainability. Continued supply also needs sufficient regeneration, suitable stand structure, and assessment of future growth and mortality. Death and harvest are different flows; dead wood can remain in the ecosystem and play other roles.

module.intro: First fix the same forest area, time period, and live-tree-volume accounting basis. Then place gross growth, mortality, and harvest separately into the inventory change, and keep single-period arithmetic distinct from long-term productive capacity.
module.diagramTitle: Why Doesn't Projected Gross Growth of 12 Automatically Make a Planned Harvest of 9 Long-Term Sustainable?
diagramSteps: Fix the proposed opening live-tree volume at 100 units and confirm that every change uses the same live-tree-volume basis
Record projected gross growth of 12 units and confirm that the 12 has not yet deducted natural mortality or harvest
Subtract projected natural mortality of 4 units to obtain projected net growth of 8 units for the proposed period
Then subtract the planned harvest of 9 units to obtain a projected ending volume of 100+12-4-9=99 units
Treat 99 as a single-period inventory result, then combine it with regeneration, stand structure, and uncertainty before deciding whether later supply arrangements need adjustment
diagramStepNotes: If forest boundaries, time periods, or live-tree classifications differ, the figures cannot simply be combined in the same inventory account.
Gross growth and net growth are not the same quantity. If net growth has already deducted mortality, mortality must not be deducted again.
Natural mortality and harvest must be recorded separately; dead trees do not thereby become additional harvestable volume.
The planned harvest of 9 is a planned removal measured on the same live-tree-volume basis, not 9 units of processed lumber or finished-product output.

A projected ending volume of 99 neither automatically proves long-term unsustainability nor proves that a fixed harvest can continue indefinitely; long-term judgment also requires regeneration and structural information.
mapping: Opening 100 → live-tree volume within the same fixed forest area at the beginning of the proposed period.
Gross growth 12 → projected addition to live-tree volume during the proposed period before mortality is deducted.
Natural mortality 4 → projected mortality leaving the live-tree inventory, recorded separately from harvest.
Planned harvest 9 → proposed removal on the same live-tree-volume basis, not processed-product output.
Staged supply confirmation → connecting the single-period inventory projection with later information on regeneration, structure, and other resource conditions.
module.boundary: The values 100, 12, 4, 9, and 99 in this example are fictional teaching projections, not measured forestry data or a real harvesting permit. Sustainable yield concerns continued supply without undermining long-term productive capacity, but a stable or nearly stable single-period inventory is not enough to prove adequate regeneration, biodiversity, or stand structure. If input data represent net growth rather than gross growth, mortality must not be deducted twice. Dead wood may continue to play other roles in the ecosystem, and this article provides no real-world guidance on removal, harvesting, or forest management operations.
module.reflection: If a new sheet reports “net growth 8” after already deducting mortality 4, how would you calculate the inventory after planned harvest 9? Why must the 4 not be subtracted again?

references.citation: Goff, T. C., et al. (2022). Iowa forests 2018: summary report. Resource Bulletin NRS-128. USDA Forest Service, Northern Research Station.
references.use: Supports distinguishing gross growth, mortality, and net growth, and supports linking sustained productive capacity with longer-term conditions such as regeneration and stand structure. This article borrows only those forest-inventory accounting concepts and long-term supply principles; it does not present the fictional teaching values 100, 12, 4, 9, or 99 as data from the Iowa report or use them to prescribe a real harvest level.

articles.summaryZh: 下一季课程原本只需重印旧路线。沈禾提前踩点，却发现多年的草地观察站已经不再是记忆中的样子。
storyParagraphsZh: 自然教育中心准备下一季的户外课程，沈禾想沿用一条已经走了多年的观察路线。其中一站一直叫“开阔草地”，学生会在那里比较低矮植物。可她提前去踩点时，原来的视野已经被灌木和几株幼树切成了几块，十几个学生再站在那里，很难看到旧记录里那片连续的草本。
她最初以为只是今年长得特别旺，便把历年的同一固定拍摄点找了出来。较早的相近季节照片里，土壤一直存在，原有多年生植物也没有全部消失；后来几年的记录中，木本幼株先零散出现在地块边缘，随后有一部分留下来并逐渐长大。照片里的变化并不是同一批草越长越高，而是地块里出现了新的成员。
沈禾继续往后翻，才看见真正改变她决定的一段过程。随着留下来的灌木和幼树冠幅扩大，原先明亮的地面出现了更多遮阴；一些过去铺得很开的喜光草本，在后来的同季节记录里只在较亮的空隙和边缘保持得更明显。也有新幼苗出现，有些早先的小木本又没有留下。她因此不再把这块地理解成“原来的草地只是长乱了”，而是把它看成同一地块里成员比例和分布正在改变。
她原来只需要把旧路线打印一遍，现在却把“开阔草地”那一站从大组活动中撤下来，改成少人数经过时观察多年变化；需要大面积比较草本的活动则移到另一处仍然开阔的地点。这样一来，课程要多走一段路，旧路线里连续多年的同地点活动也被打断了一部分。
正式带队前一天，沈禾把新路线卡夹到胸牌后面，又独自走到旧观察点。树影已经越过地上那块褪色的木桩标记，旁边一小片亮处仍长着低矮草本。她站在历年照片的取景位置拍下新的一张，没有拔掉木桩，只把路线卡上的箭头改向了下一站。
articles.overallZh: 这篇在讲：同一地块的群落组成会随着不同植物的存活、到达、建立和相互作用而改变；后来者形成的遮阴等条件又会影响哪些植物更容易继续存在。
explanationParagraphsZh: 本例用同一固定地点、相近季节的多年记录，区分“同一株长大”与“群落组成改变”。新出现的木本个体有一部分留下来，冠层扩大又改变近地受光，一些喜光草本的相对丰度和分布因而可能改变。
木本新个体可以来自后来到达的种子，也可以来自原有种子萌发或再生；仅凭这些照片，不能把其来源分开。
这些记录支持一种可理解的机制，但不能证明遮阴是唯一原因，也不能排除气候、管理历史或其他环境变化的作用。这里保留了土壤和原有根系，因此并非从裸地开始；后续路径也不必是单一直线，更不保证最终一定形成森林。

moduleZh.intro: 先固定同一地点和相近季节，再追踪谁到达、谁建立、谁留下，以及这些成员如何改变后来者经历的条件。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 为什么同一块地会从以草本为主，逐渐变成灌木和幼树更多
diagramSteps: 固定同一小地块和相近季节的多年记录，避免把季节差异或取景变化当成长期组成变化
观察到原有草本仍在，同时新的木本个体先后出现，其中一部分存活并逐渐长大
随着部分灌木和幼树长大，近地面出现更多遮阴和空间占用
在较暗条件下，一些喜光草本在地块中的相对丰度和分布减少，同时仍有新个体建立或消失
据此把变化理解为群落组成持续调整，而不是固定阶段表或必然通向某个最终群落
diagramStepNotes: 同地点和相近季节能减少明显观察偏差，但不能排除所有气候、管理或其他环境因素。
种子到达不保证建立；原有种子也可能萌发，存活植物也可能再生。照片中的新个体不直接证明其种源来自地块之外。
遮阴只是本故事中可追踪的一种作用机制，不是唯一可能驱动因素。
这里描述的是同一地块内物种或功能群的相对丰度和分布变化，不是说原来的草本主动移动到亮处。
生态演替没有统一时间表，也不保证所有地点最后形成森林。
mapping: 固定木桩与同一取景点 → 让多年记录指向同一地块。
后来出现并留下的木本个体 → 记录显示组成在改变，但没有直接确定其种源。
扩大后的灌木和幼树冠层 → 改变近地光照和空间条件。
喜光草本在亮处更明显 → 群落相对组成和分布随条件改变。
旧点保留但课程移位 → 人物承认地点在变化，同时继续长期记录。
moduleZh.boundary: 本篇只解释同一地块群落组成随时间改变的一个机制入口。固定地点、相近季节的照片不能单独证明所有因果，气候、管理、扰动历史和其他环境因素也可能参与。保留土壤、根系或存活植物后，变化不必从裸岩开始；演替也没有统一直线、固定年表或永久终态，更不表示所有地点最终都会变成森林。

articles.title: New Shadows at the Old Stop
articles.summary: The next course was meant to reuse the old route. When Shen He checks the familiar grassland stop, it no longer looks like the place in the earlier records.
storyParagraphs: The nature education centre is preparing its outdoor course for the next season, and Shen He wants to reuse an observation route that has been followed for years. One stop has always been called the “open grassland,” where students compare low-growing plants. But when she visits the site in advance, shrubs and several young trees have already broken the old view into separate patches, making it difficult for a group of more than ten students to see the continuous herbaceous cover shown in the earlier records.

At first she thinks perhaps this year has simply been unusually vigorous, so she retrieves the multi-year photographs taken from the same fixed point. In the earlier photographs from similar seasons, soil is already present and the original perennial plants have not all disappeared. In later years, woody seedlings first appear sparsely along the edge of the plot, after which some remain and gradually grow. The change in the photographs is not simply the same grasses becoming taller; new members have appeared in the plot.

As Shen He continues through the later records, she sees the sequence that actually changes her decision. As the surviving shrubs and young trees expand their crowns, more shade appears on ground that was once bright. Some light-demanding herbaceous plants that had previously spread broadly are, in later records from comparable seasons, more conspicuous only in brighter gaps and along the edges. New seedlings also appear, while some woody plants that had established earlier do not remain. She therefore stops thinking of the site as “the old grassland that has simply grown untidy” and instead sees the proportions and distribution of members within the same plot as changing.

She had expected only to print the old route again. Instead, she removes the “open grassland” stop from the large-group activity and keeps it as a small-group stop for observing long-term change; the activity that requires a broad area for comparing herbaceous plants moves to another location that is still open. The course now requires a longer walk, and part of the continuity of the long-running activity at the old site is interrupted.

The day before leading the group, Shen He clips the new route card behind her badge and walks alone to the old observation point. The tree shadows have already crossed the faded wooden stake on the ground, while a small bright patch beside it still holds low-growing herbaceous plants. Standing at the same viewpoint used in the archive photographs, she takes a new picture. She leaves the wooden stake in place and changes only the arrow on the route card so that it points to the next stop.
articles.overall: This article explains that community composition within the same plot can change as different plants survive, arrive, establish, and interact, while conditions created by later arrivals, such as increased shade, can in turn affect which plants are more likely to persist.
explanationParagraphs: This example uses multi-year records from the same fixed location and similar seasons to distinguish individual growth from a change in community composition. Some newly visible woody plants persist, and their expanding crowns alter near-ground light, which can affect the relative abundance and distribution of light-demanding herbs.
New woody growth can come from incoming seeds, previously present seeds, or regrowth; these photographs alone cannot distinguish those origins.

These records support one understandable mechanism, but they do not prove that shade is the only cause or exclude effects from climate, management history, or other environmental changes. Soil and existing roots remain present in this example, so the change does not begin from bare ground. The later pathway also need not follow a single straight line and is not guaranteed to end in forest.

module.intro: First hold the location and season broadly comparable, then trace who arrives, who establishes, who remains, and how those members alter the conditions experienced by later organisms.
module.diagramTitle: Why Can the Same Plot Shift from Herb-Dominated to Having More Shrubs and Young Trees?
diagramSteps: Use multi-year records from the same small plot and similar seasons so that seasonal differences or viewpoint changes are not mistaken for long-term compositional change
Observe that original herbaceous plants remain while new woody individuals appear, some persist, and they gradually grow
As some shrubs and young trees grow, more shade and space occupation develop near the ground
Under darker conditions, some light-demanding herbaceous plants decline in relative abundance and distribution within the plot, while new individuals continue to establish or disappear
Interpret the result as an ongoing adjustment in community composition rather than a fixed stage sequence or an inevitable path toward one final community
diagramStepNotes: Using the same location and similar seasons reduces obvious observational confusion but does not exclude every influence from climate, management, or other environmental factors.

Seed arrival does not guarantee establishment; existing seeds can also germinate and surviving plants can regrow. A newly visible individual does not by itself prove that its seed came from outside the plot.
Shade is one traceable mechanism in this story, not the only possible driver.

The story describes changes in relative abundance and distribution of species or functional groups within the same plot; it does not mean the original herbaceous plants actively move toward brighter places.
Ecological succession has no universal timetable and does not guarantee that every site will eventually become forest.
mapping: Fixed wooden stake and repeated viewpoint → keeping the multi-year records tied to the same plot.
Woody individuals that appear and persist → evidence of changing composition, without direct identification of their seed source.
Expanding shrub and young-tree crowns → changing near-ground light and space conditions.
Light-demanding herbaceous plants becoming more evident in brighter areas → community composition and distribution changing with local conditions.
Keeping the old site while moving the course activity → acknowledging that the site is changing while continuing the long-term record.
module.boundary: This article explains only one entry point into how community composition changes over time within the same plot. Photographs from a fixed site and similar seasons cannot by themselves establish every causal relationship; climate, management, disturbance history, and other environmental factors may also contribute. Where soil, roots, or surviving plants remain, change need not begin from bare rock. Succession also has no universal straight line, fixed timetable, or permanent endpoint, and it does not mean every site will ultimately become forest.
module.reflection: If shrub abundance stopped increasing in later years and a new disturbance reopened a large amount of light space, would you expect the previous direction of change to continue automatically? Why or why not?

references.citation: National Park Service, Kenai Fjords National Park. (2020, January 21, updated). Plant Succession.
references.use: Supports that plant-community composition changes over time, that surviving organisms, soil, seed arrival, shading, and competition can affect later arrivals after disturbance, and that succession does not stop permanently at one final state. This article does not adopt the page's regional species sequence or time scale and does not present the fictional trail story as NPS field data.

references.use: Supports that climate and disturbance can affect plant establishment, that surviving organisms, regeneration, seed dispersal, and canopy shading can alter community pathways, and that site history influences later change. This article borrows only those general relationships, does not transfer southwestern U.S. species or fire intervals into the fictional site, and does not use the source to claim that all succession leads to forest.
